records.name: Tabernacle
records.distinguisher: the portable tent-sanctuary Israel made at Sinai and carried through the wilderness (EXO 25:8-9)
records.notes: The LORD told Moses to have Israel make him a sanctuary after the pattern shown on the mount, that he might dwell among them (EXO 25:8-9). It was a frame of acacia boards hung with ten curtains of fine linen, covered by a tent of goats' hair and coverings of skins, with a veil dividing the holy place from the most holy (EXO 26:1-33); Bezaleel, Aholiab and the wise-hearted workmen made it (EXO 36:1-38), and Moses set it up on the first day of the first month of the second year, when the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD filled it (EXO 40:17, 40:34-35). The Levites carried it and camped round about it (NUM 1:50-53), and in the land it was set up at Shiloh (JOS 18:1). In David's and Solomon's day it stood at the high place at Gibeon (1CH 21:29; 2CH 1:3), until the priests brought it up with the ark into Solomon's temple (1KI 8:4); PSA 78:60 says God forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh. Stephen and Hebrews recall it as made after the pattern shown to Moses (ACT 7:44; HEB 8:5; 9:1-8).

records.name: Golden Lampstand
records.distinguisher: the seven-lamp lampstand of beaten gold that stood in the tabernacle's holy place (EXO 25:31-40)
records.notes: Moses was told to make it of a talent of pure gold, beaten work: a shaft with six branches, three on each side, with bowls made like almonds, knops and flowers, and seven lamps (EXO 25:31-39); Bezaleel made it so (EXO 37:17-24). It stood in the tent of the congregation on the south side, over against the table, outside the veil (EXO 26:35; 40:24-25). Aaron was to keep its lamps burning before the LORD from evening to morning with pure beaten olive oil (EXO 27:20-21; LEV 24:1-4), lighting them so that they gave light in front of it (NUM 8:1-4). On the march the Kohathites carried it wrapped in a cloth of blue and a covering of badgers' skins (NUM 4:9-10). The text does not say what became of it; Solomon made ten lampstands of gold for the temple (1KI 7:49), and Hebrews names the lampstand first among the furnishings of the holy place (HEB 9:2).

records.name: Table of Showbread
records.distinguisher: the gold-overlaid acacia table in the holy place on which the bread of the presence was set (EXO 25:23-30)
records.notes: It was made of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit broad and a cubit and a half high, overlaid with pure gold, with a crown and border, rings and staves, and dishes, spoons, covers and bowls of gold (EXO 25:23-29; 37:10-16). Leviticus orders twelve cakes of fine flour in two rows with pure frankincense, set out anew every sabbath and eaten by Aaron and his sons in the holy place (LEV 24:5-9); on the march it was covered with blue and the continual bread stayed on it (NUM 4:7). For the temple Solomon made a table of gold, and Chronicles speaks of ten tables (1KI 7:48; 2CH 4:8, 4:19); Hebrews names the table and the bread in the holy place (HEB 9:2). records.name: Altar of Incense

records.notes: It was a cubit long and a cubit broad, two cubits high, with horns, overlaid with pure gold, with a crown of gold, rings and staves (EXO 30:1-5; 37:25-28), and so it is also called the golden altar (EXO 39:38; 40:26; NUM 4:11). It stood before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony (EXO 30:6; 40:5, 40:26). Aaron burned sweet incense on it every morning and evening; no strange incense, burnt offering or drink offering was to be put on it, and once a year atonement was made on its horns with blood (EXO 30:7-10), as the blood of the sin offering for the priest or the congregation was put on its horns (LEV 4:7, 4:18). records.name: Ark of the Covenant
records.distinguisher: the gold-overlaid chest of acacia wood made at Sinai to hold the tablets of the testimony (EXO 25:10-22)
records.notes: It was a chest of acacia wood two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half broad and high, overlaid with gold within and without, with a crown of gold, four rings and staves that were not to be taken out, and the mercy seat with two cherubim above it; the testimony was put inside and the LORD would speak from above the mercy seat (EXO 25:10-22; 37:1-9). Deuteronomy has Moses say he made an ark of acacia wood and put the second tablets in it (DEU 10:1-5). It went before Israel in the wilderness, the Jordan stood still when the priests bearing it stepped in, and it was carried round Jericho (NUM 10:33-36; JOS 3:14-17; 6:11-13). The Philistines took it, Dagon fell before it, and after seven months it was sent back and stayed at Kirjathjearim (1SA 4:11; 5:1-4; 6:1; 7:1-2) until David brought it into the city of David (2SA 6:1-17). Solomon's priests brought it into the most holy place of the temple, and there was nothing in it but the two tablets of stone (1KI 8:6-9); Josiah told the Levites to put it in the house Solomon built (2CH 35:3). Jeremiah says the day would come when it would not be remembered or made again (JER 3:16), and John saw the ark of his covenant in the temple of God in heaven (REV 11:19).

records.name: Aaron's Rod
records.distinguisher: the rod of Aaron that became a serpent before Pharaoh and budded before the testimony (NUM 17:8)
records.notes: Before Pharaoh Aaron cast down his rod and it became a serpent, and it swallowed up the rods of the magicians (EXO 7:9-12). When the princes of the tribes each brought a rod, Aaron's name was written on the rod of Levi, and on the morrow it had budded, bloomed and yielded almonds (NUM 17:2-8). The LORD had it brought back before the testimony to be kept as a token against the rebels (NUM 17:10), and Hebrews places it in the ark of the covenant (HEB 9:4), though at the dedication of Solomon's temple the ark held only the tablets (1KI 8:9). records.name: Tablets of the Covenant
records.distinguisher: the two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God, on which the ten commandments were given (EXO 31:18)
records.notes: On Sinai the LORD gave Moses two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone written with the finger of God on both their sides (EXO 31:18; 32:15-16). Coming down and seeing the calf, Moses cast them out of his hands and broke them beneath the mount (EXO 32:19; DEU 9:17). The LORD had him hew two more like the first and wrote on them the words of the covenant, the ten commandments (EXO 34:1-4, 34:28; DEU 10:1-4), and Moses put them in the ark he had made (DEU 10:5). When Solomon's priests brought the ark into the temple there was nothing in it but these two tablets (1KI 8:9; 2CH 5:10), and Hebrews lists them among its contents (HEB 9:4). The text calls the second pair 'like unto the first' (EXO 34:1), and this record holds both pairs.

records.name: Solomon's Temple
records.distinguisher: the house of the LORD that Solomon built in Jerusalem and the Babylonians burnt (1KI 6:37)
records.notes: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in the fourth year of his reign, in the month Zif, the four hundred and eightieth year after the exodus (1KI 6:1), on mount Moriah in Jerusalem, at the threshing floor of Ornan (2CH 3:1). It was sixty cubits long, twenty wide and thirty high, of stone made ready before it was brought, lined with cedar and overlaid with gold (1KI 6:2, 6:7, 6:15-22), and Hiram of Tyre cast its bronze work (1KI 7:13-47); it was finished in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, after seven years (1KI 6:38). At the dedication the priests brought the ark into the oracle and the cloud filled the house of the LORD (1KI 8:6-11). Later kings emptied its treasuries and repaired it (1KI 14:26; 2KI 12:4-14; 22:3-7), and Nebuzaradan burnt it in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar (2KI 25:8-9), breaking up its bronze and carrying it to Babylon (2KI 25:13-17). The old men at the founding of the Second Temple had seen this 'first house' (EZR 3:12).

records.name: Second Temple
records.distinguisher: the house of God rebuilt at Jerusalem after the exile and finished in the sixth year of Darius (EZR 6:15)
records.notes: Cyrus king of Persia decreed in his first year that the house of the LORD be built again at Jerusalem, and returned the vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken (EZR 1:1-11; 6:3-5). In the second year of their coming Zerubbabel and Jeshua began the work and the builders laid the foundation, while old men who had seen the first house wept (EZR 3:8-12). Opposition stopped the work until the second year of Darius (EZR 4:24); at the word of Haggai and Zechariah it began again (EZR 5:1-2; HAG 1:14), and the house was finished on the third day of Adar in Darius' sixth year and dedicated with offerings (EZR 6:15-17). Haggai asked who had seen the house in its first glory and promised that the glory of the latter house would be greater (HAG 2:3, 2:9), and Nehemiah's covenant bound the people to its service (NEH 10:32-39). The text of the Old Testament does not describe its end.
